skill.name: reactome-database
skill.description: Use Reactome REST APIs and a Python helper script to query pathway data, run enrichment analysis, map identifiers, inspect disease pathways, and build browser links.
skill.summary: Query Reactome pathways and run gene or expression enrichment workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most high and medium static alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, API reference URLs, and Reactome /dev documentation paths. Confirmed issues are expected outbound Reactome API use and one helper-script output write that can persist or overwrite analysis results. No prompt injection attempt or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The helper script writes results to a path derived from the input filename.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit output path or refuse overwrites unless the user passes an overwrite flag.

remediation.issue: Live analysis submits identifiers, expression rows, search terms, and tokens to reactome.org.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy note before live queries and support a dry-run mode that shows the target endpoint.

remediation.issue: Reactome HTTP requests do not specify timeouts in the helper script.
remediation.suggestion: Add request timeouts and concise error messages for failed or slow API calls.

static_findings.snippet: Store and reuse analysis tokens to avoid redundant computation:
**For detailed API endpoints and parameters**, refer to `references/api_reference.md` in this skill.
Map identifiers to human pathways exclusively using the `/projection/` endpoint:
- `pathways`: Array of enriched pathways with statistical metrics
This skill includes `scripts/reactome_query.py`, a helper script for common Reactome operations:
- Analysis tokens are valid for **7 days**

content.user_title: Analyze Reactome Pathways from Gene Lists
content.value_statement: Pathway analysis requires reliable access to Reactome endpoints and result formats. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through pathway lookup, enrichment analysis, token retrieval, and result review.
actual_capabilities: Explains Reactome Content Service and Analysis Service endpoints.
Shows how to query pathway entities, reactions, species, and database version.
Guides overrepresentation analysis for gene or protein identifier lists.
Describes expression data submission requirements and result fields.
Provides a Python helper script for common Reactome lookup and analysis commands.
Builds Reactome Pathway Browser URLs from analysis tokens.
limitations: Requires network access to reactome.org for live API results.
Reactome analysis tokens expire after seven days.
The helper script supports common queries, not every Reactome endpoint.
Submitted gene or expression data is processed by the external Reactome service.

use_cases.title: Prioritize enriched pathways
use_cases.description: Analyze a gene list and identify significant pathways with p-values and FDR values.

use_cases.title: Map genes to pathway context
use_cases.description: Query pathway IDs, participating molecules, and related entities for annotation work.

use_cases.title: Review disease mechanisms
use_cases.description: Explore disease-related pathways and create browser links for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Check the database version
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the Reactome database version and explain which API service you used.

prompt_templates.title: Plan gene enrichment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this gene list: TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, MYC. Plan an overrepresentation analysis and summarize the expected result fields.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a pathway
prompt_templates.prompt: Query pathway R-HSA-69278, list participating entity types, and explain how to inspect the full Reactome response.

prompt_templates.title: Design an expression workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a workflow for expression TSV analysis, token reuse, FDR filtering, and Pathway Browser review. Include privacy and output-file safeguards.

output_examples.input: Gene list with TP53, BRCA1, EGFR, and MYC
output_examples.output: A ranked pathway summary with matched identifiers, top enriched pathways, p-values, FDR values, and a browser review link.
A pathway profile containing the display name, species, entity types, participating molecules, and notes for follow-up analysis.
A validation checklist for TSV format, submission steps, token handling, and significance filtering.

best_practices: Confirm that gene lists may be sent to reactome.org before running live analysis.
Cache analysis tokens and results for reproducibility while respecting the seven-day token window.
Filter pathways by FDR and review biological context before drawing conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not submit sensitive clinical data without approval.
Do not treat pathway enrichment as proof of causation.
Do not overwrite local files when saving analysis results.

faq.question: Does this skill require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. Live queries use Reactome Content Service and Analysis Service at reactome.org.

faq.question: Can it analyze expression data?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes TSV requirements and submission through the Analysis Service.

faq.question: Does it install software automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents optional reactome2py use and includes a helper script.

faq.question: What data leaves my environment?
faq.answer: Identifiers, expression rows, search terms, pathway IDs, and tokens may be sent to Reactome when live queries run.

faq.question: How long do analysis tokens last?
faq.answer: Reactome analysis tokens are documented as valid for seven days.

faq.question: Can Codex use the helper script?
faq.answer: Yes, when the runtime has Python, requests, and network access to reactome.org.
